title: Father, to Thee My Soul I Lift
description: Father, to Thee My Soul I Lift in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 435.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, to thee my soul I lift, My soul on thee de-pends, Con-vinced that ev-ery per-fect gift From thee a-lone de-scends.

lines: Father, to thee my soul I lift,
My soul on thee depends,
Convinced that every perfect gift
From thee alone descends.
Mercy and grace are thine alone,
And power and wisdom too;
Without the Spirit of thy Son
We nothing good can do.
We cannot speak one useful word,
One holy thought conceive,
Unless, in answer to our Lord,
Thyself the blessing give.
His blood demands the purchased grace;
His blood's availing plea
Obtained the help for all our race,
And sends it down to me.
Thou all our works in us hast wrought;
Our good is all divine;
The praise of every virtuous thought,
And righteous word, is thine.
From thee, through Jesus, we receive
The power on thee to call,
In whom we are, and move, and live;
Our God is all in all!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
